newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia TRI says seals deal with Deutsche Telekom.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia TRI says seals deal with Deutsche Telekom.

text.p: Malaysia's Technology Resources Industries Bhd said on Tuesday it had finalised its alliance with Deutsche Telekom.
The two companies had earlier announced that Deutsche would acquire around 20 percent of the Malaysian telecommunications firm.
"The strategic telecommunications alliance between Technology Resources Industries Berhad (TRIO) and Deutsche Telekom AG was closed today," TRI said in a statement.
A TRI spokesperson said Deutsche Telekom had finalised its purchase of 68.07 million new shares of TRI stock at 9.25 ringgit a share. That represents about 10 percent of TRI's new share capital.
Deutsche has said it also intends to purchase another 11 percent of TRI's shares from the open market. TRI shares on Tuesday closed down 75 cents to 6.70 on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
The two companies announced the alliance in June and said at the time that Deutsche would pay 9.50 ringgit each for the new shares.

"Our partnership with Deutsche Telekom facilitates and accelerates the transfer of technology. It strengthens our existing solid platform across all spectrums of telecommunications services and significantly builds Malaysia's global competitiveness," the statement said.

Deutsche Telekom is Europe's largest telecommunicaitons company and the third largest carrier worldwide. It is expected to bring its expertise in fixed line networks to TRI, which has licenses to set up fibre optic networks, cellular phone and international gateway services.
